vector: SEATS + TEAMS — axis 2 of the model. A SEAT is the per-year join: one row per driver per season, binding a driverId to the team they drive for THIS year. A TEAM is the constructor. Ruled in the F1 Racetracks App Decision Log, J10.
why_a_seat: `team` is a PER-YEAR binding, not identity. Sergio Perez is at Cadillac in 2026 and was not before; Carlos Sainz is at Williams. That is the SAME shape as circuit × weekend (J9) — a timeless thing bound to a season by a join — and the second instance is what proves it is the app's spine rather than a one-off.
no_driver_table_yet: There is deliberately NO timeless DRIVER table (name, nationality, number). One season of data does not justify a cross-season identity file, and an empty abstraction invites someone to fill it. Split SEAT into DRIVER + SEAT the day a 2025 store exists. J10 ruling 1.
canonical_for: DISPLAY — team tone, the short display name, and the driver→team binding for a season. It is NOT canonical for what happened: the `driver` and `team` strings on each classification row stay, because they are the historical record of who drove for whom THAT DAY and they are what let a round file be read standing alone. J10 ruling 2.
join: driverId. It is the only stable handle on a person in this store, exactly as slug + cuTaskId are the only stable handles on a round. Never join on a name string.
tone_vs_theme: `themeSlug` points at the NATIVE palette in shared/themes/f1/<slug>.json — a full four-vector-compatible colour entity, the real thing. `tone` is the app's LOCAL identity layer: one hex that rides on top of whatever theme is active and is never swept into a theme vector (an architecture rule this app already had for its 20-series colours). Two different jobs, deliberately both present.
tone_null_is_deliberate: ⚠️ audi, haas and cadillac carry `tone: null` ON PURPOSE and render the neutral fallback, which is exactly what they do today — no behaviour changes. All three native palettes EXIST, and all three lead with red or gold against a board where Ferrari already owns red (#FF5A60) and McLaren owns orange (#FF9B3B). Picking three distinguishable tones is an AESTHETIC decision and Michael's instruction was to ship up to that line and stop. Do not fill these in without his call.
no_code_field: ⚠️ A three-letter code field (LEC / HAM / VER) was scoped and REFUSED. Only seven codes are verifiable inside this repo (module 14's REPLAY_DATA uses RUS, PIA, HAM, NOR, VER, ANT, LEC); the other fifteen would have been invented. The store's canon rule is sourced or absent, and this app has already been scored once for exactly one fabricated dataset. `short` ships instead — it is DERIVED from the stored full name, not guessed, and it exists as a field so a two-word surname can be corrected in one place instead of breaking a regex.
maintenance: A mid-season driver change is ONE edited row here. It does not touch a single round file — past results keep the team string that was true on the day.

teams.note: THE DEAD-KEY FIX. This tone already existed in module 09's TEAM_COLORS under the keys `AstonMartin` and `Aston` — neither of which any data file writes. The store says `Aston Martin`, with a space, so the lookup missed and the team rendered neutral. Pure defect, no aesthetic choice involved.

provenance: Every driverId, full name and team string was read out of f1-results/2026/r09-silverstone.json at HEAD 08f04af — 22 drivers, 11 teams, exactly two seats per team. Nothing here was typed from memory or from an external source: this file is a normalization of strings the store already contains, which is why it can be verified by diffing it back against any round file.
